full_name.description: The candidate's full name. The person this research is FOR. Used for source discovery via WebSearch and to confirm a fetched page is about this candidate, not a same-named person.

state.description: 2-letter state code (e.g. NC). Used to disambiguate the right person/jurisdiction during discovery.

city.description: City / jurisdiction name, or null. Used to disambiguate the right person during discovery.

office_name.description: Readable office the candidate is running for (e.g. 'Fayetteville City Council'). Disambiguates the right race during discovery.

prior_roles.description: Prior public roles / offices the candidate has held (e.g. 'School Board Member 2018-2022'), to seed record and statements research. Optional; may be empty.

website_url.description: Optional hint: the candidate's campaign website. When present, fetch it directly; when null/absent, discover via WebSearch.

social_urls.description: Optional hints: the candidate's public social-media profile URLs. Used as starting points for the public footprint.

coverage_urls.description: Optional hints: known news-coverage URLs about the candidate. Used as starting points; the agent still discovers more via WebSearch.

findings.description: One entry per verified vulnerability in the candidate's own public record. A finding is emitted ONLY when its source_extract literally appears on the fetched source_url. Findings that fail verification are dropped, never invented. The array may be empty when nothing surfaced.

claim.description: The vulnerability stated plainly: what an opponent could attack the candidate on, grounded in the candidate's own public conduct.

source_url.description: The page actually fetched (the broker's returned X-Source-URL after any redirect). Every finding is grounded in a real fetched URL.

source_extract.description: A verbatim passage from the fetched page that substantiates the claim. MUST appear literally on source_url (verified via verify_quote).

category.description: Which vulnerability category this finding belongs to.

drafted_response.description: A short, ready-to-use response the candidate could give if attacked on this. First person or neutral; honest, not spin.

source_title.description: Optional human-readable title of the source page.

occurred_at.description: Optional date the underlying event occurred (not the retrieval date), or null when undated.
